mainTopic: How much of a שינוי is needed for food preparation on יום טוב: blowing chaff, crushing spices and salt, and pounding in a mortar
overview: This amud opens with the end of an earlier view: on יום טוב one may blow chaff off kernels only while holding them on the fingers. The scholars of ארץ ישראל mock this, and רבי אלעזר's ruling replaces it: blow with one hand, even with full strength. A new משנה then brings a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about crushing spices and salt on יום טוב. The גמרא notes that both sides require a שינוי for salt. רב הונא and רב חסדא give two reasons why, and the גמרא shows where those reasons differ: when the cook knew his dish in advance, and in the case of saffron. שמואל allows even salt to be crushed normally. The גמרא explains that he follows רבי מאיר, who says salt crushed together with spices needs no change, while salt crushed alone still needs one. Stories about רב אחא ברדלא tilting the pestle and רב ששת recognizing the sound of a pestle show this rule in practice. Finally, a ברייתא about טיסני and the mortar is analyzed. אביי concludes that טיסני is forbidden even in a small mortar, while ordinary pounding is forbidden only in a large one.

steps.title: Blowing chaff using only the upper finger joints
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an earlier explanation. One may blow chaff off kernels on יום טוב only while holding them from the finger joints and up.
steps.simpleTranslation: …from the joints of his fingers and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a statement that began on the previous amud. It explains how a person may blow away chaff on יום טוב in a changed way: he holds the kernels on his fingers, not in his palm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing chaff away resembles the מלאכה of זורה (winnowing), so a שינוי is needed. This view says the required change is holding the kernels on the fingers instead of the whole hand.

keyTerms.meaning: and upward, meaning toward the fingertips
a change from the normal weekday way of doing an action

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a sentence from the previous page, about separating kernels from chaff on יום טוב.

phrases.english: from the joints of his fingers and above.
phrases.notes: He holds the grain on his fingers, not in his palm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing chaff on יום טוב is permitted only while holding the kernels on the fingers, from the joints upward.

steps.title: The scholars of the West mock the finger-joint rule
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל laugh at this view. If he is already doing it differently, why not allow the whole hand too?
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West (ארץ ישראל): since he is changing the normal way anyway, it should be allowed even with the whole hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars in ארץ ישראל attack the finger-joint rule from Step 1. They find it illogical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that the finger-joint limit makes no sense. If some change is happening anyway, using the whole hand should also count as a change. So limiting it to the fingers is an arbitrary line.

keyTerms.meaning: they laughed at it (mocked the view)
in the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
since he is doing it with a change

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West:
since he is making a change,
even with the whole hand should also be allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of Step 1's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule limiting blowing to the finger joints and up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a change is being made anyway, the whole hand should be just as acceptable. So the finger limit is arbitrary.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: blow with one hand, with full strength
steps.stepSummary: The rejected view is replaced with רבי אלעזר's ruling: one may blow using one hand, even with all his strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: he blows with one hand, and with all his strength.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא throws out the finger-joint view. The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר's ruling as the correct way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real change is using one hand instead of two. Once he uses one hand, he may blow as hard as he wants. This is because the act no longer resembles normal winnowing.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (rejects the earlier view and replaces it)

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted ruling: blowing chaff on יום טוב is done with one hand (the שינוי), and then even with full force. It is not limited to the fingertips.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
he blows with one hand,
and with all his strength.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the mocked view with the accepted ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may blow chaff on יום טוב with one hand, even with full strength.

steps.title: בית שמאי: spices with a wooden pestle, salt with a flask or ladle
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with בית שמאי. Spices may be crushed with a wooden pestle. Salt may only be crushed with a flask or a pot ladle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: spices are crushed with a wooden pestle, and salt with a flask or with a pot ladle.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about crushing spices and salt on יום טוב. בית שמאי require a change for both, and a bigger change for salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For spices, בית שמאי want a small change: wood instead of the normal stone pestle. For salt, they demand a very unusual tool, such as a clay flask or a ladle. So salt gets stricter treatment.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Beit Shammai say:
spices are crushed with a wooden pestle,
and salt with a flask or with a pot ladle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, spices need a small change (a wooden pestle), and salt needs a big change (a flask or ladle).

steps.title: בית הלל: spices the normal way, salt with a wooden pestle
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל allow spices to be crushed the normal way with a stone pestle. Salt needs only the small change of a wooden pestle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: spices are crushed in their normal way, with a stone pestle, and salt with a wooden pestle.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the מחלוקת. בית הלל are more lenient for both spices and salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For spices, בית הלל require no change at all. For salt, they still require a change, but only a small one: wood instead of stone.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: spices need a small change, salt a big one. בית הלל: spices need no change, salt a small one. Either way, salt is stricter than spices.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
spices are crushed in their normal way,
with a stone pestle,
and salt with a wooden pestle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing, more lenient opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, spices need no change, and salt needs only a small change (a wooden pestle).

steps.title: Everyone agrees that salt needs a change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out the common ground: both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a change for salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: In any case, everyone agrees that salt needs a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes what both sides agree on: salt can never be crushed the normal way on יום טוב. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the lenient בית הלל, who let spices be crushed normally, still require a change for salt. That makes salt stand out, and it raises the question of why it is treated more strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: at any rate, in any case

phrases.english: GEMARA:
according to everyone, at any rate,
salt requires a change.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת מֶלַח בָּעֲיָא שִׁנּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the point both sides of the משנה agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a שינוי for crushing salt.

steps.title: Why does salt need a change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason salt, unlike spices, always needs a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why salt is treated more strictly than spices. The answers come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spices and salt are both seasonings crushed for cooking, so they seem alike. The גמרא wants to know what is different about salt.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the agreement in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why salt needs a change while spices (at least for בית הלל) do not.

steps.title: First answer: every pot needs salt, so prepare it beforehand
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says every dish needs salt, so a person should have crushed it before יום טוב. Not every dish needs spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא: one said, all pots need salt, but not all pots need spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two אמוראים about the reason. This step gives the first answer; the second answer continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since everyone knows every dish needs salt, a person could and should have crushed it before יום טוב. If he did not, he may do it on יום טוב only with a change. Spices are not needed in every dish, so he may not have known in advance that he would need them, and they may be crushed normally.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key principle for יום טוב: work that could easily have been done before יום טוב is treated more strictly, and so it needs a שינוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the first opinion appears here. We are not told whether it belongs to רב הונא or רב חסדא, and the second opinion comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:
one said:
all pots, every one of them, need salt,
but not all pots need spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 with the first of two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Salt is needed for every dish, so it should have been prepared before יום טוב. Spices are not always needed, so a person may not have foreseen needing them.

steps.title: Second reason: spices lose flavor, salt does not
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא explains that spices lose their flavor if crushed early, but salt keeps its flavor. So salt could have been crushed before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: All spices lose their flavor, but salt does not lose its flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second side of the disagreement between רב הונא and רב חסדא. It gives a different reason why salt always needs a change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spices crushed before יום טוב would go flat, so a person had a good excuse to wait. Salt stays strong, so he could have prepared it the day before. Since he did not, he must use a change on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: They lose their flavor (the taste fades)

phrases.english: And the other one said:
All spices lose their flavor,
but salt does not lose its flavor.
phrases.notes: So salt could have been crushed before יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided answer started in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Salt keeps its flavor, so it should have been crushed before יום טוב. Spices lose their flavor, so they could not be prepared early.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two reasons would lead to different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for a real case where the two reasons would give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons agree that salt needs a change and ordinary spices do not. So the גמרא wants a case where the two reasons actually split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? A standard question asking for the practical difference between two opinions

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two reasons from steps 8 and 9 differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where 'not every dish needs spices' and 'spices lose flavor' lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: knowing the dish ahead of time, or saffron
steps.stepSummary: The reasons differ when a person already knew which dish he would cook. They also differ in the case of saffron, which keeps its flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when he knew which dish he wanted to cook. Or else, the difference is with saffron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the two reasons lead to different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case 1: He knew which dish he would cook. By the 'not every dish needs it' reason, he knew which spices he needed, so he should have prepared them early and must use a change. By the 'loses flavor' reason, he still could not prepare them early, so he needs no change. Case 2: Saffron does not lose its flavor, so by the 'loses flavor' reason it needs a change. By the 'not every dish needs it' reason, saffron is like other spices and needs no change.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
A pot, meaning a cooked dish
Saffron, a spice whose flavor does not fade quickly

steps.whatToRemember: The two reasons for salt's special rule are: every dish needs salt, and salt keeps its flavor. They split when the cook knew his dish in advance, and in the case of saffron.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where he knew which dish he wants to cook,
phrases.notes: He could have known which spices he would need.

phrases.english: or else, in the case of saffron.
phrases.notes: Saffron keeps its flavor, like salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reasons differ when the cook knew his dish in advance, and in the case of saffron.

steps.title: שמואל: everything may be crushed normally, even salt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: anything that is normally crushed may be crushed in the usual way on יום טוב, even salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: All things that are crushed may be crushed in their normal way, and even salt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought. It seems to let salt be crushed with no change at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the גמרא said that both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a change for salt. שמואל's ruling seems to say the opposite, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are crushed or pounded

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
all things that are crushed may be crushed in their normal way,
and even salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling that seems to clash with step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything that is normally crushed, including salt, may be crushed in the usual way on יום טוב.

steps.title: But we said salt needs a change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. We already saw that everyone agrees salt needs a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that salt needs a change?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling because it seems to contradict what was just learned from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the גמרא pointed out that both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a change for salt. שמואל allows salt with no change, so he seems to go against both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? This introduces a contradiction
A change, meaning doing the act in an unusual way

phrases.english: But didn't you say that salt needs a change!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12 using the agreement noted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that salt may be crushed normally.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that both בית שמאי and בית הלל require a change for salt. So how can שמואל allow it with no change?

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי מאיר: salt crushed with spices needs no change
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows a ברייתא where רבי מאיר says there was no dispute about crushing spices normally with salt mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches. רבי מאיר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about things that are crushed. Those may be crushed in their normal way, with salt together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל follows a different version of the dispute, taught by רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, salt crushed together with spices is fine with no change at all. So שמואל's 'even salt' means salt mixed in with the spices. Salt crushed by itself is a separate case.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא, following a specific opinion from the time of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think שמואל allows salt by itself to be crushed normally. His 'even salt' means salt crushed together with the spices.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how שמואל can rule against the plain reading of our משנה. He relies on רבי מאיר's version of the dispute.

phrases.english: He said it in accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about things that are crushed, that they may be crushed in their normal way
with salt together with them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a different תנא (רבי מאיר's version of the dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל goes against both בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי מאיר, who says salt crushed together with spices needs no change according to everyone.

steps.title: The real dispute: crushing salt by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the dispute was only about salt crushed alone. בית שמאי allow it only for roasting. בית הלל allow it for anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagreed about crushing salt by itself. בית שמאי say: salt may be crushed with a flask or a wooden ladle for roasting, but not for a pot. בית הלל say: with anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains what בית שמאי and בית הלל actually argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow only a small amount of salt, enough for roasting, and only with a change. They do not allow the larger amount needed for a pot. בית הלל's words 'with anything' look like they allow any tool, which the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasting, which needs only a little salt

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא לְדוּכָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: They only disagreed about crushing it by itself,
as Beit Shammai say:
salt may be crushed with a flask or with a wooden ladle for roasting,
but not for a pot.
And Beit Hillel say: with anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא לְדוּכָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt crushed by itself: בית שמאי allow it only for roasting, with a flask or ladle. בית הלל allow it 'with anything.'

steps.title: Could בית הלל really allow any tool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. Could בית הלל really allow salt to be crushed with any tool, with no change?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With anything'? Can that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It does not make sense that בית הלל allow crushing salt alone with no change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is already clear that salt by itself needs a change. If בית הלל allowed any tool, there would be no change at all. So the wording 'בכל דבר' cannot be right as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? Used to show an idea is unthinkable
With anything, meaning with any tool

phrases.english: 'With anything'? Can that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of בית הלל's view in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'בכל דבר' in בית הלל's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt crushed alone needs a change, so בית הלל cannot allow any tool at all.

steps.title: Correct the reading: 'for anything'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes one letter. בית הלל mean 'for anything,' meaning for any dish, still using a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: for anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא to answer the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בכל דבר' (with any tool) becomes 'לכל דבר' (for any purpose). Now בית הלל still require some change when crushing salt by itself. They just allow it for any dish, whether roasting or a pot, unlike בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. This introduces a corrected reading
For anything, meaning for any purpose or dish

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, salt crushed with spices needs no change, and שמואל follows this. Salt crushed alone always needs a change. בית שמאי allow it only for roasting, while בית הלל allow it for any dish.

phrases.english: Rather, say: for anything.
phrases.notes: For any dish, roasting or a pot, but still with a change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל allow salt alone to be crushed with any tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל allow salt alone for any dish, but still with a change.

steps.title: רב אחא ברדלא tells his son to tilt the pestle
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא ברדלא instructs his son that when crushing salt on יום טוב, he should tilt the pestle to the side and then crush.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא ברדלא said to his son: When you crush salt, tilt the pestle to the side, and then crush.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life instruction that shows how people actually followed the rule from Step 17. Salt may be crushed on יום טוב, but only with a change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 concluded that בית הלל allow crushing salt for any dish, but only with a שינוי. Here we see what that change looks like in practice: you crush at a slant instead of straight down. This makes it look different from a normal weekday job.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gave his son practical instructions

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּרְדְּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Acha Bardela said to his son:
When you crush (salt), tilt it to the side and then crush.
phrases.notes: The tilt is the 'change' (שינוי) required for salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּרְדְּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical form of the שינוי required in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt is crushed on יום טוב only with a change: tilt the pestle to the side.

steps.title: רב ששת hears a pestle and says it is not from his house
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת hears the sound of a pestle on יום טוב and says it cannot be coming from his own household.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת heard the sound of a pestle. He said: This is not coming from inside my house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story about crushing salt with a change. רב ששת was sure his household would not crush salt the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had taught his household to crush salt only with a שינוי. When he heard a pestle being used normally, he concluded it must be some other house. This story sets up the next two questions, which ask how he could be so sure.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (known to have been blind, so he relied on hearing)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet heard the sound of a pestle,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הַאי לָאו מִגַּוֵּויהּ דְּבֵיתַאי הוּא.
phrases.english: He said: This is not from inside my house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story supporting the rule that salt needs a change.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A normal, unchanged pounding of salt is not done on יום טוב; רב ששת's household would not do it.

steps.title: Maybe they were tilting the pestle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the pounding רב ששת heard was being done with a tilt, the allowed way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they were tilting it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. How did רב ששת know the pounding was forbidden? Maybe it was being done at a tilt, which is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pounding was done at a tilt, it would be fine, and it could even have come from his own house. So hearing a pestle alone does not prove anything wrong was happening.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were tilting it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion רב ששת drew in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's certainty that the pounding was forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pounding with a tilt is allowed, so the sound alone may not show anything wrong.

steps.title: The sound was clear, so it was not tilted
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת heard that the sound was clear and sharp, which happens only with straight pounding.
steps.simpleTranslation: He heard that its sound was clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a tilted pestle makes a dull sound, but this sound was clear. So רב ששת knew it was being pounded the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straight pounding and tilted pounding sound different. A clear, ringing sound means straight pounding, with no change. That is why רב ששת knew it was not allowed.

phrases.english: Because he heard that its sound was clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail: the kind of sound tells how the pounding was done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the pounding was tilted and allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clear sound shows straight pounding, with no change.

steps.title: Maybe they were crushing spices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe they were crushing spices, which may be crushed normally on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it was spices?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. Spices may be crushed normally on יום טוב, so maybe that is what רב ששת heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא we learned that spices may be crushed in the normal way. So even a clear sound of normal pounding might be perfectly fine if it came from spices, not salt.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were (crushing) spices?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב ששת's certainty, after Step 21 answered the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's conclusion that the pounding was forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spices may be crushed normally, so a clear sound could come from allowed spice-crushing.

steps.title: Spices make a barking sound
steps.stepSummary: Crushing spices makes a dull, barking sound, which is different from the sound of salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spices: their sound is like barking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that spices sound different when crushed. They make a dull, barking sound, so רב ששת would have known if it was spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each material makes its own sound under a pestle. The clear sound he heard was not the barking sound of spices. So it must have been salt crushed with no change.

keyTerms.meaning: Barks like a bark (a dull, barking sound)

steps.whatToRemember: Salt on יום טוב must be crushed with a change, like tilting the pestle. רב ששת could tell by the sound that salt was being crushed normally, and not tilted or spices.

phrases.english: Spices: their sound is like barking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22 and closes the רב ששת story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail: spices make a different sound
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the clear sound came from allowed spice-crushing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spices make a barking sound, so the clear sound must have been salt.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids making groats and pounding in a mortar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב one may not make טיסני (crushed grain) and may not pound in a mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not make טיסני, and one may not pound in a mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא about crushing grain on יום טוב. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טיסני is wheat crushed into pieces, which takes a lot of work. The ברייתא lists two rules: no making טיסני, and no pounding in a mortar. The next step asks why two rules are listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Mortar (bowl for pounding with a pestle)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not make groats,
and one may not pound in a mortar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic: crushing grain on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, no making טיסני and no pounding in a mortar.

steps.title: Why are two rulings listed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the ברייתא lists two separate rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. Why list two separate rules when they seem to be about the same thing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: טיסני is made in a mortar anyway. Also, saying only 'no טיסני' suggests other things may be pounded, but then the ברייתא says no pounding in a mortar at all. The two rules do not seem to fit together as separate items.
steps.confusionAlert: תרתי here is not counting for its own sake. It is a challenge: why does the ברייתא list two separate rulings?

phrases.english: Two (rulings)?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of two separate rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two rules overlap or seem to contradict, so they should not be listed as separate items.

steps.title: The second ruling is the reason for the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא means: you may not make טיסני because you may not pound in a mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: Why may one not make טיסני? Because one may not pound in a mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is really only one rule. The second part gives the reason for the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא should be read as a reason, not as a list. טיסני is forbidden because making it requires pounding in a mortar, and that is forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
What is the reason one may not make groats?
Because one may not pound in a mortar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the second clause is the reason for the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one ruling with its reason: no טיסני because no mortar.

steps.title: Then just say no pounding in a mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if that is the meaning, the ברייתא should simply say 'no pounding in a mortar' and skip טיסני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it just say: One may not pound in a mortar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the real rule is 'no mortar,' why mention טיסני at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no mortar is allowed, then of course no טיסני can be made. Saying 'no mortar' would already include it. So mentioning טיסני seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it say (why not just say)

phrases.english: Then let it say: One may not pound in a mortar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in Step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'No mortar' already covers טיסני, so naming טיסני seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Mentioning groats teaches that even a small mortar is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Without naming טיסני, we might think only a large mortar is forbidden. Naming טיסני teaches it is forbidden even with a small mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it taught only 'no pounding in a mortar,' I would think that applies only to a large mortar, but a small mortar is fine. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why טיסני had to be mentioned. It shows that making טיסני is forbidden in any mortar, even a small one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large mortar looks like a weekday job, so we might think only that is forbidden. A small mortar might seem fine. By saying 'no טיסני' at all, the ברייתא teaches that it is forbidden no matter the size of the mortar.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the ברייתא is read as forbidding טיסני because it needs a mortar, and it names טיסני to show that even a small mortar is forbidden. Step 30 revises this reading.

phrases.english: If it had taught (only) 'one may not pound in a mortar,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּמַכְתֶּשֶׁת גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: I would have said: this applies only to a large mortar,
but with a small mortar —
I would say it is fine,
so it teaches us (that it is forbidden).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי תָּנֵי אֵין כּוֹתְשִׁין בְּמַכְתֶּשֶׁת, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27. This answer is itself challenged in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why extra wording is needed (to block a mistaken idea)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a large mortar is forbidden; a small mortar is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Making טיסני is forbidden in any mortar, even a small one.

steps.title: Another teaching permits a small mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion that pounding is forbidden even in a small mortar. It cites a ברייתא that forbids only a large mortar and explicitly permits a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: one may not pound with a large mortar, but one may pound with a small mortar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to contradict what we just concluded. That ברייתא permits pounding in a small mortar on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said that naming טיסני teaches that even a small mortar is forbidden. This new ברייתא openly allows a small mortar. So the two sources appear to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? This phrase opens a challenge from an outside source.
A large mortar, used for big batches
A small mortar, used for small amounts

phrases.english: But it was taught: one may not pound with a large mortar,
phrases.notes: The challenge opens with a quote from a different ברייתא.

phrases.english: but one may pound with a small mortar!
phrases.notes: This is the clause that clashes with Step 28.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 28 by citing a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from Step 28 that pounding is forbidden even with a small mortar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא permits a small mortar. Therefore the first ברייתא cannot mean that a small mortar is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: the mortar ruling refers to a large mortar
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the first ברייתא's ban on pounding in a mortar was taught about a large mortar. So the ברייתא really contains two separate rulings. טיסני is forbidden even in a small mortar, and general pounding is forbidden only in a large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When that ברייתא was taught as well, it was taught about a large mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. The 'no pounding in a mortar' clause of the first ברייתא refers only to a large mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא is read as two separate laws, not one law with its reason. The first law is that making טיסני is forbidden even with a small mortar. The second law is that pounding other things is forbidden only with a large mortar. This matches the second ברייתא, which permits a small mortar for ordinary pounding.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, a leading אמורא of Babylonia
When it was taught too, meaning the other teaching is to be understood this way as well
A teaching. Here it refers to the first ברייתא.

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, making טיסני is forbidden even with a small mortar. Ordinary pounding is forbidden only with a large mortar and permitted with a small one.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say טיסני is permitted in a small mortar. Only ordinary pounding is permitted in a small mortar. טיסני stays forbidden in both sizes.
steps.whyThisMatters: The first ברייתא is understood as two independent rulings. This gives the practical rule for mortars on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When that teaching was taught as well,
phrases.notes: This refers to the first ברייתא about טיסני and the mortar.

phrases.english: it was taught about a large mortar.
phrases.notes: The 'no pounding' clause is limited to a large mortar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תַּנְיָא נָמֵי מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 29 by limiting the scope of the first ברייתא's mortar clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a clause. The first ברייתא is read as two separate rulings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ברייתא forbids all mortar pounding, even with a small mortar, which would contradict the second ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: טיסני is forbidden even in a small mortar. General pounding is forbidden only in a large mortar, so the two ברייתות agree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Small mortar: permitted for ordinary pounding but forbidden for טיסני. Large mortar: forbidden for all pounding.
